report:
Finding: Model B appears biased toward a journalistic/institutional register (news/sports/legal/medical reporting) relative to Model A, especially at the very start of a sequence.

Why I think this:
- Signal location: The difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 across mid-to-late layers, consistent with a shift in “document start/lede” style rather than a narrow skill (e.g., math).
- Logit-lens vocabulary at pos0 evolves into advisory/news-lede language: Stay, Every, Sustainable, Consider, rejected, normal/human/relevant, “, recommend, Do/Non/Check, optimize/ensure/adhere, proactive/mindful, coming/upcoming. This reads like headline/lede/guidance phrasing common in institutional/news copy.
- Later positions (pos2–pos4) repeatedly surface news-domain nouns and frames: law/Law, tragic/tragedy, surgeon/clinic/surgery, Royals/Manny (sports), Herald/Visit, downturn, wrong/incorrect. These clusters are typical of legal/medical/sports news articles.
- Pos1 often shows later/latter/ago/mention/visits/trips—time and referential markers common in reportage.

Caveat: Patchscope readouts weren’t provided, so this inference rests on the consistent logit-lens patterns and the strong BOS-position concentration. If this is not an intended domain shift, I cannot identify a more specific objective from the evidence.
